caption: A lightning bolt hits the metal rod on top of a tall building, and the rod and roof flash bright for an instant.

sa.check: A tall building with a metal rod on top.
A lightning bolt comes down to the rod.
The rod and the roof flash bright for an instant.
The bolt ends at the rod, not elsewhere on the roof or on the building's side.
The order is bolt, flash, dark.

pc.expect: The bolt appears and is gone; the rod and roof return to their unlit look and stay so.
pc.fail: The bolt stands as a steady lit line for the rest of the clip; or the rod glows on after the bolt is gone; or the bolt's foot creeps along the roof; or the flash fades in slowly.

pc.expect: The building, its rod and the skyline are the same before and after the strike.
pc.fail: The rod vanishes or bends after the strike; or a second rod or building appears; or the roof line changes between dark and lit frames; or the building changes place.

pc.expect: The bolt is a jagged, branching line whose main channel ends at the tip of the rod.
pc.fail: The bolt is a straight beam or a smooth arc; or a wide glowing tube; or it ends at a point in mid-air beside the rod while the rod lights up.

pc.expect: The flash lights the surroundings: the roof, nearby facades and the cloud undersides brighten during the bolt, lit from the bolt.
pc.fail: The bolt is visible while the roof and nearby facades stay as dark as before; or the street below is lit while the roof beside the rod stays dark; or the roof brightens with no bolt present.

pc.expect: The bolt ends at the rod and does not pass through the roof into the building; the building stays solid.
pc.fail: The bolt continues down through the roof and lights the floors inside like lamps; or the roof opens or caves in; or the bolt passes through the building's wall; or the rod sinks into the roof.

pc.expect: The facade's colour, the windows' lit pattern and the sky keep their look apart from the flash.
pc.fail: The facade changes colour rather than brightness; or the lit windows change pattern all at once; or the sky turns to daylight after the flash.
